title: With birth as condition, bhikkhus, aging and death come to be. With existence as condition, bhikkhus, birth comes to be. With clinging as condition, bhikkhus,…
content: With birth as condition, bhikkhus, aging and death come to be. With existence as condition, bhikkhus, birth comes to be. With clinging as condition, bhikkhus, existence comes to be. With craving as condition, bhikkhus, clinging comes to be. With feeling as condition, bhikkhus, craving comes to be. With contact as condition, bhikkhus, feeling comes to be. With the six sense bases as condition, bhikkhus, contact comes to be. With name-and-form as condition, bhikkhus, the six sense bases come to be. With consciousness as condition, bhikkhus, name-and-form comes to be. With formations as condition, bhikkhus, consciousness comes to be. With ignorance as condition, bhikkhus, formations come to be. Whether Tathāgatas arise or do not arise, that element still persists, that stableness of Dhamma, that fixed course of Dhamma, that specific conditionality. The Tathāgata fully awakens to this, fully realizes it. Having fully awakened to it, having fully realized it, he declares, teaches, proclaims, establishes, reveals, analyzes, clarifies, and illuminates it.

title: Furthermore, bhikkhus, in the future there will be bhikkhus who are undeveloped in body, undeveloped in virtue, undeveloped in mind, undeveloped in wisdom. Because they…
content: Furthermore, bhikkhus, in the future there will be bhikkhus who are undeveloped in body, undeveloped in virtue, undeveloped in mind, undeveloped in wisdom. Because they are undeveloped in body, undeveloped in virtue, undeveloped in mind, undeveloped in wisdom, the elder bhikkhus will live in abundance, lazy, leaders in decline, discarding the burden of seclusion, not making an effort to attain what has not been attained, to achieve what has not been achieved, to realize what has not been realized. And later generations will follow their wrong view. They will become those who live in abundance, lazy, leaders in decline, discarding the burden of seclusion, and will not make an effort to attain what has not been attained, to achieve what has not been achieved, to realize what has not been realized. Thus, bhikkhus, from defilement of the Dhamma comes defilement of the Discipline; from defilement of the Discipline comes defilement of the Dhamma. This, bhikkhus, is the fifth fear regarding the future, not yet arisen now but will arise in the future. You should fully understand them. Having fully understood them, you should strive to abandon that fear.

title: Like the moon unstained Moving through the firmament, With radiance blazing Among the starry host in the world. So too, one of virtue, A person…
content:
Like the moon unstained
Moving through the firmament,
With radiance blazing
Among the starry host in the world.
So too, one of virtue,
A person with faith,
With giving, blazes forth
Among the stingy in the world.
Like a cloud with rain and thunder,
A garland with a hundred crests,
Filling up the valleys,
Spreading over the plains.
So too, full of vision,
A disciple of the Perfectly Enlightened One,
The wise one surpasses stinginess
In five respects:
Life span and fame,
Beauty and happiness,
With abundant wealth,
Upon death he enjoys heavenly bliss.

title: - What illuminates the world? What awakens the world? Who works together with humans? What is their conduct? Who nourishes both the lazy and the…
content:
- What illuminates the world?
What awakens the world?
Who works together with humans?
What is their conduct?
Who nourishes both the lazy and the diligent,
Like a mother her child?
What beings sustain their lives
Depending on the earth?
- Wisdom illuminates the world,
Right mindfulness awakens the world,
Cattle work together with humans,
The plough is their path.
Rain nourishes both the lazy and the diligent,
Like a mother her child.
Rain sustains beings' lives,
Depending on the earth.

title: And, bhikkhus, what is the practice of restraint? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, when seeing a form with the eye, does not grasp the general sign,…
content: And, bhikkhus, what is the practice of restraint? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, when seeing a form with the eye, does not grasp the general sign, does not grasp the particular sign. For whatever reason, if the eye faculty were unrestrained, covetousness, grief, evil unwholesome states might arise, he restrains that cause, guards the eye faculty, practices the restraint of the eye faculty. When he hears a sound with the ear... smells an odor with the nose... tastes a taste with the tongue... feels a touch with the body... cognizes a mind-object with the mind, he does not grasp the general sign, does not grasp the particular sign. For whatever reason, if the mind faculty were unrestrained, covetousness, grief, evil unwholesome states might arise, he restrains that cause, guards the mind faculty, practices the restraint of the mind faculty. This, bhikkhus, is called the practice of restraint.

title: The Blessed One: Like a bull breaking its bonds, Like an elephant tearing rotten creepers, I will not enter a womb again. So if you…
content:
The Blessed One:
Like a bull breaking its bonds,
Like an elephant tearing rotten creepers,
I will not enter a womb again.
So if you wish, O deva of rain, let it rain!

title: And, bhikkhus, what is adherence to local language and excessive use of everyday speech? Here, bhikkhus, in various regions, people know words for 'dish', 'bowl',…
content: And, bhikkhus, what is adherence to local language and excessive use of everyday speech? Here, bhikkhus, in various regions, people know words for 'dish', 'bowl', 'cup', 'plate', 'pot', 'basin', 'vessel'. Thus, as they know these words in those regions, someone insists, clings, and says: 'Only this is true; everything else is false.' Thus, bhikkhus, is adherence to local language and excessive use of everyday speech. And, bhikkhus, what is non-adherence to local language and non-excessive use of everyday speech? Here, bhikkhus, in various regions, people know words for 'dish', 'bowl', 'cup', 'plate', 'pot', 'basin', 'vessel'. Thus, as they know these words in those regions, a person, without clinging, explains: 'They, depending on this, speak thus.' Thus, bhikkhus, is non-adherence to local language and non-excessive use of everyday speech.

title: Bhikkhus, if one were to speak rightly about Sāriputta, one could say: 'Sāriputta is the legitimate son of the Blessed One, born of his mouth,…
content: Bhikkhus, if one were to speak rightly about Sāriputta, one could say: 'Sāriputta is the legitimate son of the Blessed One, born of his mouth, born of the Dhamma, fashioned by the Dhamma, an heir of the Dhamma, not an heir of material things.'

title: Reflecting wisely, he uses lodging only to ward off cold, to ward off heat, to ward off the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and…
content:
Reflecting wisely, he uses lodging only to ward off cold, to ward off heat, to ward off the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and creeping things, only to remove the dangers of climate, and only for the purpose of seclusion and quietude.
Reflecting wisely, he uses medicines and medical requisites only to ward off arisen painful feelings and for the sake of complete freedom from affliction.
Bhikkhus, if he did not use thus, harmful, afflicting taints might arise; but when he uses thus, those harmful, afflicting taints do not arise. These, bhikkhus, are called taints that are to be abandoned by using.

title: 'One who clings, bhikkhu, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One.' - 'Venerable Sir, I understand. Well-Gone…
content: 'One who clings, bhikkhu, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One.' - 'Venerable Sir, I understand. Well-Gone Sir, I understand.' - 'How, bhikkhu, do you understand in detail the meaning of my brief statement?' - 'Venerable Sir, one who clings to form is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One. One who clings to feeling ... to perception ... to formations ... to consciousness is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One. Venerable Sir, this is how I understand in detail the meaning of the Blessed One's brief statement.' - 'Good, good, bhikkhu! It is good that you understand thus the meaning of my brief statement. One who clings to form, bhikkhu, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One. One who clings to feeling ... to perception ... to formations ... to consciousness is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One.'
